# 1. 

## a.

> The Fisher sharp null hypothesis assumes that class size makes exactly no difference in the outcome. In other words, it assumes that each class would have gotten the exact same result regardless of class size, small or regular. 

## b.

To make this table as an object in R, 

```{r}
#| label: 1a-setup
#| message: FALSE

library(tidyverse)
library(survey)

# elongate table so each row is a class
## (so we don't have to deal with columns w/ vectors)

school = c(rep(1, 2),rep(2, 2),rep(3, 2),rep(4, 2),rep(5, 2),rep(6, 2),
           rep(7, 2),rep(8, 2),rep(9, 2),rep(10, 2),rep(11, 2), rep(12, 2), 
           rep(13, 2), rep(14, 2),rep(15, 2), rep(16, 2), rep(1, 2),rep(2, 2),
           rep(3, 3),rep(4, 2),rep(5, 2),rep(6, 2),rep(7, 2),rep(8, 4),
           rep(9, 2),rep(10, 2),rep(11, 2), rep(12, 3), 
           rep(13, 2), rep(14, 2),rep(15, 2), rep(16, 2))

w_i = c(rep(0, 32), rep(1, 36))


reg = c(-0.197, 0.236, 0.117,1.190,-0.496,0.225,-1.104,-0.956,-0.126,
        0.106,-0.597,-0.495,0.685,0.270,-0.934,-0.633,-0.891,-0.856,
        -0.473,-0.807,-0.383,0.313,0.474,0.140,0.205,0.296,0.742,0.175,
        -0.434,-0.293,0.355,-0.130)

small = c(0.165, 0.321, 0.918, -0.202, 0.341, 0.561, -0.059, -0.024,
          -0.450, -0.258, -0.083, 1.151, 0.707, 0.077, 0.371, -0.870,
          -0.496, -0.444, 0.392, -0.568, -1.189, -0.727, -0.580, -0.533,
          0.458, 1.001, 0.102, 0.484, 0.855, 0.509, 0.618, 0.978, 
          -0.545, 0.234, -0.240, -0.150)

y = c(reg, small)

tps = tibble(
  school = school,
  w_i = w_i,
  y = y
)
```


From Section 9.4.2, denoting our number of strata as $J$, then for some $J$-component vector $\lambda$, we have statistic


$$
T^{dif, \lambda} = \left|~\sum_{j=1}^{J} \lambda(j) \cdot \left(\bar{Y}_t^{obs}(j)-\bar{Y}_c^{obs}(j)\right)\right|; \quad \lambda(j) = \frac{N(j)}{N} 
$$


$$
T^{dif, \lambda_{RSS}} = \left|~\sum_{j=1}^{J} \frac{N(j)}{N} \cdot \left(\bar{Y}_t^{obs}(j)-\bar{Y}_c^{obs}(j)\right)\right|
$$

To compute for the observed data, using the following formula and code:

$$
T^{dif, \lambda_{RSS}} = \left|~\sum_{j=1}^{16} \frac{N(j)}{N} \cdot \left(\bar{Y}_t^{obs}(j)-\bar{Y}_c^{obs}(j)\right)\right|
$$

```{r}
#| label: 1b-obs-test

n_class = tps |> nrow()

T_obs = tps |>
  group_by(school) |>
  summarize(
    y_t = sum(w_i * y),
    y_c = sum((1-w_i) * y),
    n_j = n()
  ) |>
  mutate(T_j = (n_j/n_class) * (y_t - y_c)) |>
  summarize(abs(sum(T_j))) |>
  pull()

paste0("The observed data gave a test statistic of approximately ", round(T_obs, 4))
```
 
## c. 

```{r}
set.seed(10)

tps_rand = tps

rand_1 = tps |> filter(school == 16) |> select(w_i) |> pull() |> sample() #randomization
indices_16 = which(tps$school == 16)
for (i in 1:length(indices_16)) {
  new_w = rand_1[i]
  tps_rand$w_i[indices_16[i]] = new_w
}


n_class = tps_rand |> nrow()

T_rand = tps_rand |>
  group_by(school) |>
  summarize(
    y_t = sum(w_i * y),
    y_c = sum((1-w_i) * y),
    n_j = n()
  ) |>
  mutate(T_j = (n_j/n_class) * (y_t - y_c)) |>
  summarize(abs(sum(T_j))) |>
  pull()

paste0("The data after randomizing the 16th school's assignment groups gave a test statistic of approximately ", round(T_rand, 4))
```
